response:
Diagnosis. The archive has converged on a single dominant architecture: a bounded non-negative capital-intensity weight on an operating-earnings-to-price leg. Its three best incarnations are the champion (dp/at lightness × five-year average operating profit to price: alpha 3.4%, t 3.55, Sharpe 0.48), the spot version (3.0%, t 3.33) and the MAX envelope (3.0%, t 2.99). Two negative lessons are now firm: adding a second bounded moderator compresses the cross-section and *lowers* alpha (durability stack 2.8%, own-norm surprise 1.3%, per-share growth 1.3%), and dynamic/rank moderators of profitability produce high Fama-MacBeth slopes with mediocre portfolio alpha. So the remaining budget is best spent on the two components of the champion that have never been varied on their own terms: what the intensity weight actually measures (asset-scaled capital consumption, revenue-scaled capital consumption, capital productivity, or an intangible business-model proxy) and the functional form of the earning-power anchor (average, conservative lower envelope, log-transformed to strip distress-driven extreme yields). Two of the six also test economically substantive validation channels rather than more grid cells.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: RevenueScaledCapitalIntensity_x_NormalizedEarningsYield
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dp, sale))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(oiadp, 5), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The economically relevant burden is capital consumption per dollar of revenue produced, not per dollar of book assets, because revenue measures the output the capital base actually generates and is immune to the write-downs and stale historical cost that distort the asset denominator.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The champion's weight is the one component never varied, and the critic's standing objection is that dp/at is a noisy proxy contaminated by asset-base accounting; scaling the same capital-consumption charge by revenue tests whether the effect is about the business model's reinvestment need or about the asset denominator. Coverage is unaffected because both inputs are already required by the champion.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: CapitalProductivity_x_NormalizedEarningsYield
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, at)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(oiadp, 5), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheapness against mid-cycle earning power pays most for firms that turn their capital over quickly, because high asset turnover means the earning power is generated by an efficient operating base rather than by a heavy, slow-moving asset stock whose returns are hostage to utilization.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Turnover and depreciation intensity are economically distinct readings of "capital-light" — one is productivity of the asset base, the other its consumption rate — and separating them tells us which mechanism drives the archive's best result. This is the sharper of the two interpretations to test because turnover is a first-order operating characteristic rather than an accounting charge, and it is measurable for every firm without additional lags.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: AssetLightness_x_ConservativeEarningPowerYield
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dp, at))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(oiadp, MA(oiadp, 5)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: A prudent valuation anchor is the lower of current and mid-cycle profit: a firm that still looks cheap on the pessimistic estimate of its earning power is cheap for real, whereas a firm that looks cheap only because a stale five-year average flatters a deteriorating business, or only because of one exceptional year, is not.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The MAX envelope (demonstrated capability) delivered 3.0% alpha and the plain average 3.4%, so the untested lower envelope directly answers whether the champion's edge comes from optimistic capability or from conservatism, and it is not recoverable from either parent since MIN is a different non-linear function of the same two inputs. Economically it screens out the two failure modes of normalization — stale averages for decliners and windfall years — using no additional data.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: FiveYearCashValidation_x_NormalizedEarningsYield
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(ib, oancf), 5), at))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(oiadp, 5), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Averaged accounting profit is only a credible measure of earning power if, over the very same five years, that profit converted into operating cash; firms that accumulated accruals over the window have a flattered average and their apparent normalized cheapness is an accounting artifact.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This matches the horizon of the conditioner to the horizon of the valuation numerator, which no prior signal does — the earlier accrual test used a single-year gap against a spot yield and produced 1.8% alpha — so it is a genuine validation mechanism rather than another quality gate. Cumulative accruals are also a stronger and more persistent predictor than one-year accruals, which is the reason to accept the coverage cost of a five-year cash-flow window.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: AssetLightness_x_LogNormalizedEarningsYield
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dp, at))), IND_ZSCORE(LOG(RATIO(MA(oiadp, 5), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Extreme raw earnings yields are produced by distress and imminent impairment rather than by mispricing, so compressing the yield logarithmically — and excluding firms whose mid-cycle earning power is not positive at all — should concentrate the spread on genuine value rather than on the deep-distress tail.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every signal in this family has relied on 1% winsorization to control a right-skewed yield, which is a blunt instrument; the log transform changes the entire shape of the long leg and simultaneously imposes the economically meaningful screen that a firm must have positive normal earning power to be called cheap. If alpha and t-alpha rise while coverage falls only modestly, the champion's long leg was being diluted by distressed extreme-yield names, which is directly actionable for the final generations.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: IntangibleIntensity_x_NormalizedEarningsYield
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(xsga, 5), at)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(oiadp, 5), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms whose competitive assets are built through expensed selling and administrative investment carry understated capital and understated profit, so when such a firm is already cheap on mid-cycle reported earnings its true economic yield is higher still and the mispricing is larger.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is a mechanism-attribution test rather than a grid cell: low depreciation intensity and high expensed-intangible intensity both identify asset-light business models, so if this pairing reproduces the champion's alpha the driver is the business model, whereas if it lands near its earlier 1.4% the driver is specifically capital consumption. That distinction determines which weight the final generations should refine, and it costs nothing in coverage relative to the five-year normalization already in use.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE RevenueScaledCapitalIntensity_x_NormalizedEarningsYield---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A single-operator denominator swap on the archive champion, but a defensible one — dp/sale is mechanically dp/at divided by asset turnover, so the test cleanly decomposes whether the champion's moderator works through capital consumption or through the asset-base denominator, though the incremental information over the champion is likely modest and the result will be highly correlated with it.

---CRITIQUE CapitalProductivity_x_NormalizedEarningsYield---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Asset turnover is a well-known DuPont-component predictor (Soliman 2008) so the leg itself is not novel, but its interaction with a mid-cycle-normalized yield is untested in this archive and economically distinct from depreciation intensity; note it is close to the reciprocal-complement of Proposal 1, so the two should be interpreted jointly rather than as independent evidence.

---CRITIQUE AssetLightness_x_ConservativeEarningPowerYield---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: MIN(oiadp, MA5) is the one remaining cell of a three-point grid whose other two points (plain average 3.4%, MAX envelope 3.0%) already produced near-identical results, so the expected incremental information is small — but the conservative anchor does correspond to a genuinely different economic screen and the expression matches the hypothesis exactly.

---CRITIQUE FiveYearCashValidation_x_NormalizedEarningsYield---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Horizon-matching the accrual conditioner to the five-year valuation numerator is a coherent and non-cosmetic upgrade on the earlier one-year accrual gate, though the leg is a straightforward long-window Sloan accrual measure, the flow-numerator/stock-denominator scaling (5-year sum over current at) is internally inconsistent in units, and the oancf plus five-year window will bite coverage.

---CRITIQUE AssetLightness_x_LogNormalizedEarningsYield---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a pure monotone re-transformation of the champion that simultaneously and silently deletes every firm with non-positive mid-cycle operating profit, so any change in alpha confounds tail compression with a large sample-selection shift — exactly the coverage-driven "apparent improvement" the objective warns against — and the stated distress story concerns the sample screen, not the log itself.

---CRITIQUE IntangibleIntensity_x_NormalizedEarningsYield---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Both legs are already in the archive (IntangibleCapitalIntensity_x_TotalCapitalEbitdaYield and the normalized earnings yield used by six prior signals), making this a mix-and-match grid cell rather than a new mechanism, and the stated attribution logic is weak since a middling result would be equally explicable by the known noisiness of accumulated-xsga proxies.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: AssetLightness_x_TroughEarningPowerYield
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dp, at))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_MIN(oiadp, 5), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Value with a margin of safety means being cheap against the profit a firm earns in its worst year, not its average year; pricing the five-year trough of operating profit against market value ranks firms by stress-tested earning power and automatically pushes firms whose worst year was a loss to the expensive end where they belong.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This achieves the distress-screening intent of the flagged proposal inside the signed valuation leg rather than by silently deleting firms, so coverage matches the champion and no sample-selection shift confounds the comparison — firms with a negative trough receive strongly negative scores instead of vanishing. It is also a distinct anchor from both the mean and the current-versus-mean lower envelope, because the trough is a worst-case order statistic that reveals cyclical fragility the average conceals.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: AssetLightness_x_NormalizedResidualEarningPowerYield
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dp, at))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(SUB(oiadp, xint), 5), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Equity owns mid-cycle operating profit only after lenders are paid, so pricing normalized operating profit against market capitalization systematically overstates the cheapness of levered firms; netting the interest bill out of normal earning power measures the residual claim shareholders actually buy, and the correction is largest precisely for the levered value names that trap value investors.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: No prior signal nets financing costs out of a normalized *equity* yield: the archive either priced operating profit against equity alone, which mismatches numerator and denominator claims, or against total capital, which prices the whole structure and so cannot identify equity-specific mispricing. Holding the capital-intensity weight fixed isolates this claim-matching correction, and it should raise both the slope and the alpha if the champion's long leg has been partly populated by levered firms whose apparent cheapness belongs to their creditors.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
